And they have been living in my camp and they have been there and we have good cooperation. But they -- I understand that they always was looking for some interest to sell to the international media. So after the 3rd, at the morning of the 4th the -- the BBC team informed me, "Thank you for your hospitality. We don't want to be any more nice. Nothing is happening here now, so we leave." And after -- I don't really remember, one hour, 30 minutes, I don't know, they came back and informed me that, "Now you have soldiers down -- from the BH army down in the south part of Vares and they have taken our food, what we have to drink, and maybe some clothes or something like this." And they also informed me what was, they called the 7th Muslim Brigade. I have never heard about that before, so I said okay. And I immediately ordered my quick-reaction platoon to be ready, and I used my APC and we get down to Vares, and I meet them in the middle of Vares more or less, that means the square about the mayor's house. And I stop my APCs, put them in a half-circle in front of the attacking unit from the 7th Muslim Brigade. And they was walking in two columns in the left and the right side of the street, what you can say more than ordinary infantry attack in this type of terrain, in urban terrain. And they was cross-firing. The left was shooting on the right; the right was shooting on the left. And they were shooting -- a lot of shooting. And I immediately get out, together with my interpreter and some guards, and I walk towards them and I was saying, "Komandant. Komandant, Put out." And one -- of them get in front of me. And I also inform my interpreter to tell them that they immediately have to stop shooting because it's no enemy here, it's no soldiers here. It's only civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened when you told this individual that.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: They was stopped shooting, and they more or less immediately start to have some celebration. They had already smashed a lot of windows, shops. They was taking chocolate. They was taking bread and so on. But they were stopped shooting. They -- I understand that they -- they understand that there was no enemy there any more. And they -- when I was talking to the soldier who say he was -- maybe it was company commander or battalion commander; I don't know. I have no sign for that. And he -- when I was talking to him with my interpreter, one of the soldiers was smashing a window, right in front of you and me now. And it was a shoe shop. I think it was only for ladies. And he was -- "Get inside there and start to take shoes." And I immediately take a step aside and point with my right hand in Swedish and say, "Stop about that and get out from this." And he do it. It was not necessary to translate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Trial Chamber the soldiers that you saw coming down the street towards you, what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. They wore -- they have a lot of green flags and they also some green band here. And some of them was singing maybe "Allah-u-ekber," and something like this. I never see this type of unit before. It was clear, what you can say, Muslims. I was very -- when I was in Bosnia, it was very important for me to don't say Muslims army. I always say BH army, because it was the BH army. But in this moment it was very, very clear it was Muslims. It was green light colour, like here, this green, and it was -- I've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay, sir, you've -- you've pointed to a model here in the courtroom. Can you please describe in words so it's reflected in the transcript the shade of green that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. It was more or less this light green colour. I mean, this type of light green colour, what you have here on this. Light green.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the flag that you -- or flags that you said these people were carrying.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. They had a flag with -- with a moon, a half -- what is sign of -- Muslim sign. And I don't remember really, but I think it was with some written words maybe. But I really don't remember what.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've told us about the soldier that you were able to stop by simply telling him to stop. Can you please continue with the story, what happened after that soldier stopped.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. I also informed the commander of this unit that he shouldn't do anything wrong with the Croat civilians who still was in Vares because they have nothing with Stupni Do to do, because in my opinion it was people outside Vares who came to do with Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, sorry to interrupt. Why did you tell this person or why did you mention the name Stupni Do in this context?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Because I was afraid they should do some revenge to the civilians -- Croatian civilians in Vares. So therefore I informed them that they have nothing to do but Stupni Do, and I also said, "You should not do anything wrong to these people. Let them go. Don't do anything wrong." But he was very tough, and he said, "Both UN, UNPROFOR, and the civilian Croats we should now push out from Vares." And I said, and pointed my APCs, "You're welcome. We can start now." And he only said [indiscernible] and then walked -- sorry -- and then walked away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you just told us about having fears that there would be some kind of revenge on the Croatian civilians in Vares. What was the basis for this fear or concern that you had?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Afterwards -- I can't understand. You mean about Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, you've told us -- and the quote from the transcript is, "I was afraid they should do some revenge to the civilians, Croatian civilians in Vares."

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. What I understand -- what I've been informed and what I have in my own opinion was that some of this, as you could call, bad soldiers in HVO who do this, they more or less killed, murdered civilians in Stupni Do and destroyed the village. And what I understand, it was no people from Vares. They came from -- they said they came from the Kiseljak area. And they also informed me that they was -- one HVO policeman told me one moment that "You must be careful about these people because they are crazy. They have a lot of revenge because they have been pushed out from Kakanj area. They have raped, maybe, and they have -- members of their family have been killed," and so on. So it could be some revenge in Stupni Do. It could also be some old business. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please, then, continue with what happened on the street in Vares as you had this discussion with the 7th Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: After the commander had walked away, after I have tell him that he was welcome to start to push me out, he don't want to do that. He walked away. And one of the soldiers asked me about the sign. It was mayor house and up, it was a sign about -- with HVO red-and-white check sign. And I understand him, together with my interpreter, he asked me if he was allowed to take this sign down. And I said, "Yes, of course, I don't have anything about that to do." But I shouldn't say that, because they shoot it down. After that they stopped shooting again. And I have a lot of informing at that moment, also from my units in Vares that there was a lot of looting in Vares. So I sent out patrols in different streets to stop looting. And they have smashed a lot of shops, a lot of bread shops -- every shop was more or less smashed, the windows were smashed. And we tried to be there and there to stop them, but it was what you can call a cat and rat game. When we was there, they stopped. And when we leave them there, they start again. So I decided to be in three points, to protect the Catholic church, because we have also starting to shooting against this; to protect the two UNHCR stores for food for civilians. And one of these stores was in a shop. They have already smashed the window. So I ordered one of my APCs to back in the back of the APC in this shop, to put out wire outside. And when I was there, with commander I have a meeting in the square there too. And he said, "You must leave us the food. Because it's all logistics. It's all logistics to take the food when we enter an area. We have no food for days and weeks and something like this," he told me. I said, "You're not allowed to do that because this food is not yours. It belongs to the UN. And if you enter that area, we are going to open fire our weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, what -- just for the record, what day and approximately what time was it where you had this discussion?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It was before lunchtime, sometime before lunchtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On which day?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: The 4th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that there was a lot of looting going on. Can you tell the Trial Chamber who was doing this looting.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: In my opinion, it was soldiers from this unit what they called was the 7th Muslim Brigade. Maybe it was soldiers from other units [Realtime transcript read in error: "our unit"] too -- I mean in BH army. I don't know. I also meet one policeman from BH army with a Kalashnikov and I tell them that you must stop them. You're a policeman. And he said, "I can't do that. I'm alone." So he don't do anything. And I understand him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When did this looting in Vares by these soldiers stop?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't really know, because we -- as I said, we concentrated at three places. We have shooting in the air to stop them, but it was impossibility for us to be everywhere the whole time. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Stop, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I believe that there is a mistake in the transcript. When the witness was talking about other units that may have been in the town and they were looting, in the transcript it says -- it should have said "from other units," page 60 -- 59, that is, and line 25. So it should read members of "other units" not "soldiers from our unit too."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I thank my learned -- I thank my learned colleague for that correction to the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, again, the question was: When did the looting by soldiers in Vares stop?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I understand it was stopped sometime after the afternoon this day, because in the same time I also was informed about that it was some massacre up in the village of Pogar, so I was up there with the patrol and we find 20 bodies of more or less old men and it was a funeral there. And my medic was observed and looked at some of them. And I think one of them or two was killing by not shoot, but it was nothing -- the civilians don't want to say anything. And under this time the Battalion commander, Colonel Henricsson, also have arrived to Vares and was down there. And he informed me in the evening when I was back from Pogar to my camp that it had been some military police there from BH army and -- stop the looting, and then maybe they also have used the weapons to stop them. I was not there that afternoon. I only have report from my soldiers and from my commander that they have stopped at -- late this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the next day or the day following that, that is, sometime on the 5th or 6th or 7th of November, 1993, did you have an opportunity to be in the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. At the evening this day, the 4th, if I remember right, it was one company from the French Battalion in Sarajevo also arrived to help us up in the area. And I have no command over these soldiers. It was under command of my -- commander, Colonel Henricsson. So he gave them orders to take positions down in Vares, to stop -- to take care, what you say, control over the city so it's no more looting, and important positions, they put them out. And I think it was this day at the evening. So it was calm there. The next day it was more or less calm in the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So when you say "the next day it was more or less calm," that would be the 5th --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: The 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The 5th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On that day, sir, were you able to personally observe the results of what had happened the previous day?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. There was -- more or less every shops was looting -- looted. And it was -- we have no -- they have no burnt down some houses or some like this. It was looting. And they have taken a lot of, also I think furniture or something like, this because I have also reporting from my soldiers up in Kopjari. I have still observation posts there. And they observed and reported to me that it was some trucks and cars with furniture and other equipment, and maybe they came from this area, or another village around Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Colonel, it's a bit unclear from the record. Did you or did you not observe houses which had been burnt down?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No. No houses down in Vares had been burnt down, only looting by shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Birger, thank you very much for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no further questions at this time for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. We still have about 15 or 20 minutes before the break. Would the Defence prefer to have a break now? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Although the Defence of General Hadzihasanovic has very few questions for this witness because the accused Hadzihasanovic is not charged with the events that took place in Vares, still, we would like to have a break now and then begin with the cross-examination after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. It is ten past 12.00. We are going to make a half-an-hour break, and we will continue at twenty to 1.00 and work for the following hour without a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. The cross-examination can begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. As I had occasion to mention earlier on, General Hadzihasanovic is not charged for the events that took place in Vares. Nevertheless, we would like to ask a few questions of this witness for the context and also for an understanding of the sector where these operations took place. And for that purpose, I should like to use the model that we have in front of us, and I would like to ask the witness if he can recognise certain locations on the model.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Colonel Birger, good day. We've had the opportunity of meeting yesterday with my colleague Mr. Dixon. Today I am in company of my colleague Mrs. Residovic and my colleague Mrs. Muriel Cauvin, and together we represent General Hadzihasanovic. As I've mentioned, we have very few questions for you. However, because you were on the terrain at that time, we would like to use your expertise and to -- if we can ask you to walk towards the model on the right side with a pointer, you will be assisted by the usher who will give you ear phones that you can hear what I'm saying as well as a pointer and I will simply ask you to point for the benefit of the Chamber to some of the areas on the model.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is the first time that we are doing this, so ... [In English] If I can ask the technical booth to put the small video camera on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Colonel Birger, if you can -- can you hear what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher -- oh, you have to have the microphone. I'm just waiting for the video booth to put the camera on so that the -- it is on? Okay. Colonel Birger, if I can ask you to look on the model and using the pointer to locate for the Trial Chamber the town of Vares.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It's here, in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I can ask you now to look at the town of Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It's up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if you can illustrate the link between Stupni Do going towards Vares.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I think it's not pointed out here, but it's two links. It was one up here or, something like this, and also one you -- came from the north, north-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I can ask you now, Colonel Birger, to look at the map and to indicate where you can see the two towns that you've mentioned earlier on; namely, Dragovici and Mijakovici.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Here is the valley. There's one name but I don't -- Orasac [phoen], so it must be south, here -- Mijakovici ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to put the microphone further back, because we see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Here you have Mijakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have the small camera again -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you locate Mijakovici and Dragovici.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: From Vares we used this road down here. And when we came here we have them on the left side on this end of this road. This must be here. And here also we have a name, I can see Mijakovici. This was inside this small valley here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And finally, Colonel Birger, if I can ask you to point at Kopjari. Now, Kopjari I know personally the name is not on that model. However, if you can point towards Ratanj.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Kopjari --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Ratanj. The town of Ratanj?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Bratanj?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Ratanj.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It's not -- I think it's a village west of Kopjari. And Kopjari must be up here on this place, something like this, because this was up on the hill and when we have Mijakovici and Dragovici down here in the valley. So someplace here you have this village, Kopjari. And west of, you have, I think, Ratanj, if I remember right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Birger, can you by looking at the model and the towns that you have just located, would you say that this model is a fair illustration of the type of terrain; namely, the mountains, the forest, and the difficulty of the roads between these areas?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. It was a lot of mountains, and the road was like serpentines up in the road. So yeah, it's very likely the terrain down in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. If you can go back to the witness seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will now ask the usher, please, to look at Exhibit DH84, which is the map of the area of Vares. DH84 is 1 to 100.000, and it's the map that bears the number 475, Vares. [Interpretation] Mr. President, for future witnesses, we are going to take the maps which are 1 to 25.000, and we are going to collate them together and make a big picture out of them, and this will cover the same area as the model represents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [In English] Colonel Birger, now, using this map, can you locate for the Trial Chamber the town of Vares, always using the pointer.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you indicate in a general area where it is located on the map so that the Judges of the Chamber can see it. About where on the map do you find it?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, have you found the same spot as the witness on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [In English] Now, from Vares, once again, Colonel Birger, can you with the pointer follow the road down to Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Here. So the road is one here and you also can use from the north. Here we have it in a small valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, again using the pointer, if you can take a look at the road leading from Vares to the two towns that you've mentioned earlier; again, Dragovici and Mijakovici.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: We used the road up the Pogar. That means here. And then the road down here to these two villages. It was also breached here where you can use on the right side up to Kopjari and then left of the bridge you came down to this Dragovici and Mijakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, on this map, Mr. Birger, we can see the town of Kopjari. Can you point at the town of Kopjari?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It's up here. And you have Ratanj here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you also point towards the town of Borovica.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. Borovica, it's bigger, a lot bigger village. It's over and down Borovica is down here, north of Kopjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Birger, am I right in saying that when there was an attack on Kopjari, that initially, the initial thrust came from Borovica?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The initial stage of the attack on Kopjari started in Borovica.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I have some report about that. But the attack, it was more what you can say to -- I don't find the English word -- to do an attack. I think that they should attack Borovica. But -- but the main attack was down in the village of Kopjari. And the attack came from the village of Mijakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying, Colonel Birger, that what happened in the area of Borovica was basically to draw the HVO into that part while the main thrust of the attack would be coming from both Mijakovici and Dragovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Maybe it was a plan like this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would it be right in saying that this was sound military planning and attack that was displayed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We can put the map aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have a few questions relating to the attack on Kopjari. You, in response to a question put to you from my colleague of the Prosecution earlier, you mentioned that the attack on Kopjari was not a matter of whether it would be attacked but actually when it would be attacked. Can you elaborate on this response.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: If I understand you right, you mean the [indiscernible] available when they attacked; yes. The [indiscernible] were available. But I understand already the day before that maybe they were going to attack because I was down in the both village, Mijakovici and Dragovici, and there were a lot of soldiers from BH army there and I have -- they are not been there -- not been there when I was there the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you confirm, Colonel that, the attack was short, effective, that fog was used as an advantage, and that it was an overall well-performed attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah, it was -- they used the fog, and they -- I can say, in my opinion, they have used good tactic in the plan, to use the terrain, to use the weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you reported in a statement that you provided the Office of the Prosecutor with that on this attack in Kopjari some casualties were reported to you, namely two dead people or three - I don't recall correctly - but those -- that those were battle casualties.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: When I arrived, I had a message from one of my officers who was commanding up in this place, that he needs help up there because there was civilians there and the attacking soldiers from the BH army tried to push them out, said they were not allowed to be there any more. So when I arrived up there, it was a lot of -- 20 civilians, maybe more -- around the APCs, old people, children. They were of course afraid. And I could also observe a lot of BH army soldiers there, some have helmets. So I understand it was more -- more professional soldiers, so to say. They were attacking soldiers. One woman said to me, crying, said, "It has been a massacre here, killed people," and so on. So I sent my military police and one of my officers to look at this place. And what I can remember, I find one soldier. He was lying in his trenches. Maybe he had been shooting against attacking and he has a bullet here somewhere. So he was only lying like this. So in my opinion, it was not massacre; it was -- he was killed in this fight. And also, one soldier was wounded and maybe the BH army soldier had tried to help him because he had some first aid here, But he was already dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That was a soldier from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who had taken care of a wounded soldier from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: What I can understand, maybe it had been in that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you yourself, Colonel, did not see the troops actually performing the attack on that day.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No. It was my platoon leader of 1st Platoon and his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And it is only later on that you were told by some soldiers within the Bobovac Brigade that actually 3rd Corps had performed this operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I -- what I can understand, it was units from the 3rd Corps, because when I was talking to -- he said he was maybe battalion commander. He informed me that -- that the civilians, Croat civilians, should not be there any more. They want to push them out. And I said no. And after some hours, they arrived some staff officers and they said they came from the headquarters of the 3rd Corps. And they said the same aim to me. They said it was not allowed to be there. And I said it was all right for them to be there because it was -- belonged to these people, and that BH army was a government army, and why should they push them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Colonel, if I mention to you that this attack could have been performed by a mix of both soldiers from 2 Corps and 3 Corps, is that -- would that be a possibility?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: You mean from -- in my opinion, it couldn't -- never been from the 2nd Corps. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, if I move on, Colonel Birger, to the events which followed, and that was on the 23rd of October. You mentioned in response to a question from my colleague an attack that took place on Stupni Do. Can you confirm that this was an attack which was performed by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. They -- that's right. They informed me about that, and they said they have -- are going to attack Stupni Do because they need the road opened on to the village of Mir. And afterwards we also could confirm that when we get into the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, when -- this attack in Stupni Do, would I be right in qualifying this attack as the worst scene during your time that you were in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that this attack would indeed qualify as a massacre?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I have -- I was not personally inside Stupni Do. It was -- my commander was there, some of my officers, and one of my platoons, and one platoon from another company in the battalion. What they described for me, it was awful. It smelled awful. They have tried to destroy the bodies, that means by put them on fire. And -- we also find -- one of my officers found three women inside in the basement under the floor. They opened the bottom, inside the house and they find three women together, shotting in the head, and so on. So it was a massacre. That's a right word about it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Colonel, if I -- am I correct in saying that you tried yourself to go to Stupni Do both the same day and the following day and you were prevented from doing so?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you insisted to go to Stupni Do for a full day, and as you mentioned to my colleague you were getting a bit impatient because of going around asking for someone to speak to, you mentioned that at some point some person from the Bobovac Brigade basically told you to take your vehicles and to go back to your compound and then from that point on you would not be allowed any kind of freedom of movement? Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And it was the 24th of -- it was Sunday, the 24th of October. I remember it very well because it's also UN Day, therefore I remember it very well. And I try -- I've been try to talk to them the whole day, and at this evening they put -- put off their earlier operation. An officer in this Bobovac Brigade. And he said, "I'm now the brigade commander." And he was very afraid. And he told me that "If you don't take -- remove your soldiers and vehicles inside your camp, we are going to destroy them and kill them. And we're also going to use snipers to shoot inside your camp," because it was very slopey down the valley. And I tell him, "If you do that, we're going to use all our equipment, all our weapons to defend. And I'm not going to move any of my units," and then I leave the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Colonel, am I right in saying that that same night the HVO actually started to shoot at your camp and that at that moment you had to take all necessary actions to respond to this threat, including telling your soldiers to shoot to kill and not to shoot to warn? Can you explain those events of that night.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. I -- about 10.00 in the evening, maybe - I'm not really sure, but about that - I have an information from one of my soldiers inside the camp that they're going to threaten my soldiers down in Vares outside the school. And I tell him to tell my soldiers we were radioed: "Don't move. We're staying there because we don't want to do anything. I don't think they are going to do that." And after the few minutes, he came back again and said, "They are doing that. And you must came." And I understand that I must go out to my staff tent. And I could in the same moment also I heard a lot of shooting down -- and also bigger smashing, like grenades, down in Vares, and it was a lot of bullets. You could see them in the air too over the hills. When I came out from the building, there also was shooting over the road, over the camp, over the head of us when I ran out to my tent . And I gave order to my -- one of my platoon leaders down in Vares, he was with his own APC, to shoot warning shoot with automatic cannon. He do that. And then they shoot more. And they also threw hand grenades through Red Cross APCs, destroyed the wheels. So we must take them away up to the camp. And I ordered him to shoot real fire with automatic cannon to defend themselves and the Red Cross APCs. But he don't do that. And I think it was right, because he had done, that had also penetrating the houses where there was civilians, so he don't do that. So we went back to position. And we use also smoke grenades, when we was backing back to a position where they don't shoot against us any more. They also threatened one APC down in -- the checkpoint up to Stupni Do, and they came out with small anti-tank weapons. And I ordered this APC to move the area and put it up to the others -- just outside, but simply say, the other side from my side of the tunnel in the north part of Vares, where we have positions for the rest of the night. And at the morning we again get down in Vares and take control over all the old positions. And there was negotiations to the Bobovac Brigade and informed them that now we should warning shoot night. We're not going to shoot warning shoot anymore. If you're shooting against me or my soldiers, we're going to open fire to shoot back. And they was very, very afraid. You could see that in his face. And they never shoot against us any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. If I move on quickly. This armed conflict that UNPROFOR and your unit was involved in with the HVO and then was also put to this conflict by a letter which had to be issued all the way up from General Petkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I can recognise that name, but I'm not -- remember his positions. I could recognise --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But do you remember, Colonel, receiving a letter saying that the Bobovac Brigade had to stop any threat, threatening action towards UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's right. We have a letter from Kiseljak, I think, about that. And for sure was some letter about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, I have a few general questions with respect to your deployment and then that will be it from me. The first question is: Of course your headquarters was located close to the Bobovac Brigade near Vares.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It's about 200 metres' distance, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you almost had daily contacts with the Bobovac Brigade, at least for the period of October and November 1993.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Kresimir Bozic is the one where initially during your deployment he drew the confrontation lines and the areas of responsibility on your map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's correct. And his position in this moment was information officer. He said so. But later, on the 24th of October, he said he was the new brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And your battalion or your company operated mostly during your complete tour, or at least again October and November, in the area of responsibility of 2 Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: 2 Corps and the area of the Bobovac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you were aware at that time, Colonel, of the history of the relationship or the previous relationship between the HVO and the ABiH, were you?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. You mean ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Were you aware of the relationship which had existed prior to those events between the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't really understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry. I will try to make my question more precise.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Were you aware that the HVO and the ABiH fought together before these events?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Maybe they have -- do that, because the 2nd Corps told my commander that the Bobovac Brigade was a part of 2nd Corps. And I was in negotiation up in Rijeka, I think it was the 2nd of November, the deputy commander of 2nd Corps also, writing his letter to the Bobovac Brigade, I came to us to more as friends. Be a part of 2nd Corps . Don't fight any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Colonel, you as a professional officer and staff-trained officer, you were aware of the strategic importance of Vares, were you?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. It -- it is the only road up to Tuzla more or less from -- it's the only road from south up to north.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you were also aware, if I'm correct, that throughout the summer of 1993 - that is, prior to your arrival - the Serbs had been attempting to cut 2 Corps from the rest of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Not in this moment. Later in November, they tried -- they attacked the area between Dastansko and Olovo in the north direction and take control over some two or three Muslims village. And we were afraid they tried to cut the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you were aware early in your deployment in Bosnia that the situation elsewhere in Central Bosnia was very tense between the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you were also aware at that time that there were even some allegations that the HVO and the Serbs were uniting their efforts with a view to defeating the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Not really. I understand when I was in Vares that there was some cooperation between the Serbs and the HVO because they used the road in Bosnian Serbs' area down to Herzegovina. That's my opinion, that they have some cooperation about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. This was my question, that the Serbs and the HVO were cooperating and that you had evidence to that effect. Now, my next question is: Of course the area you were in was very mountainous and forested areas with peaks, as we have seen from the model. Do you agree that the communications in this context was a very difficult endeavour, even though you yourself managed to be in constant contact with your headquarters in Tuzla using satellite and radio communications?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. We have problems with radio communications. We have also put out an observation point in the village of -- oh, I don't remember the name, but it is a mountain west of Olovo. We have an observation post to try to have radio contact. But mostly in the beginning or more or less the whole time we used the satellite telephone to have a contact to the battalion headquarters in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, Colonel, the satellite telephone that you had available was not available to either the HVO or the ABiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that we used them to -- to -- some other parts. We only used in negotiation with the HVO and the BH army. But we never via radio or via satellite telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you're not aware that they had such equipment allowing them to communicate faraways.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I suppose they had. But from what I remember, we never used this communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if the HVO or the ABiH had some -- this type of equipment, it would have been held mostly with the most -- more senior commanders. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. We -- I know that my -- the staff, the battalion staff up in Tuzla, have some contact with -- with fax and so on, when we tried to deploy the unit inside Bosnia even directly with Palewej [phoen] sometimes. But we never have it in my level.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, you mentioned in response to one of the questions that towards the end of October there was a situation which developed in Vares whereby more than 200 Muslims were held in a school. I'm not sure I got all the situation as it happened. Can you elaborate a bit more on what happened and what you did exactly in response to these events.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It was also Sunday the 24th. We tried, as I said before, to come into the Stupni Do. We tried to talk to the Bobovac commanders. But we have no success about that. So I -- in that moment, I used my car and some of my soldiers and we went up the road up to Pogar. That means west of Vares, to try to look over the village, over the mountains down in Stupni Do, because we could see smoke over the hills. And when I was there, staying there, there came a woman - maybe she was about 50 years old - and she could speak a little German, and she informed me that it was hundreds of men, Muslims, between twenty years to old men inside the school and she described the place, the school. And I understand the place. I immediately take my car, went down to Vares. And if you are in -- at the square, you have the mayor house. On the right of the mayor house, you have that school. And when you are looking in this direction, behind you you have the police station. So I went into the police station, and I think I say like this, "You know and I know what's happening inside this school. I want to have a list of the prisoners." And immediately they gave me a list. And every name have a number, and I could follow immediately through the papers, and I think it was 233 names on this paper. But it was only some seconds. And immediately he take it back again, because I think he understand he had done a mistake to show it to me. And I also -- there I want to talk to the commanders again. He said they was out in terrain. There was no police chief, no military commanders, nobody to talk to. So I remember I was very angry, took my helmet, and threw it very hard into the table and said, "Now, I want to talk to one commander." And he was afraid, one of the policemen, and he used the telephone to try to talk to the commander. And I could hear from the phone that they were angry that he had called him. So I understand that it was no meaning to be there any more. So I left, and it had been dark outside. And when I came out, one of my soldiers called me and said, "You must come here. We have some people here who want to talk to you." And behind the Red Cross APC, one Red Cross and one ordinary APC were -- it was two HVO soldiers. One, he has a red cross here. It was some type of medic. And he could speak English and he informed me that inside this school there's going bad things there, and he also asked me if I was the highest UN commander in Vares. And I said, "For the moment, yes." And he said, "You must do something. Because it's my friends. I'm from Vares. But don't say it. I have to say something." And then he walked away into a side street. And in that moment I decided to have one APC there. I don't want to be provocative, so I put one Red Cross APC there, only to observe and report. I went back to the Bobovac Brigade. And when I meet the new brigade commander, only in this moment he said to me to take all my units inside my camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, just for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, can you confirm that when you mentioned the word "APC" you referred to an armoured personnel carrier, which is a track vehicle that carries anywhere from seven to ten soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: This type, I have -- on the platoons, it was tracks APC, personnel carrier APCs. But the Red Cross APC was on wheel; they have no weapons. And the APC I used for my commanding APCs, it was not there. That one was in Pancevo. So I used a wheeled APC. And it was not from my company. It was from some guard platoon from the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Colonel, can you confirm that towards the end of October, early November the HVO blocked a humanitarian convoy which wanted to go through Vares and that this is the reason why the mayor of Tuzla actually came to Vares, to try and get this convoy to travel to Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't really know why he was in -- from Tuzla was down in this area. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But are you aware, Colonel, that there was a humanitarian convoy which was prevented from travelling through Vares by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe because it was convoys more or less every day. And I remember it was in this evening when I have met him, when I was going back to Vares and it was a bridge between the two different parts. But in this moment this was no longer the line, because it was moved south directions. But this bridge where I still have a checkpoint, and I was not allowed to use a bridge. And there was also part of 10th Mechanised Coy there and I was going down to my area and I was going back Rijeka again and had a paper from the commanding of 2nd Corps to get down there. If it was some humanitarian convoys, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Colonel. I have almost finished with my questions. You've mentioned a lot of details of the attacks which were led by BiH soldier and you qualified them as being professional attacks. Would you agree with me that the nature of the operations, the military operations in that area during the time frame from late October to early November would have necessitated coordination at the very high level of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't know how they coordinated, because as my commander informed me, the 2nd Corps was a little afraid for the 3rd Corps because in this moment the 2nd Corps also have, as I say before, attacked from the north to the south, and they was afraid to meet the 3rd Corps in Vares. So they also ask him if we could be between with two -- our corps in the same army. But it was not our mission to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But as a professional officer, Colonel, if you say that 7 Brigade was involved into an operation, Vares, which is in the 2nd Corps, you know as a professional officer that this requires authority or permission from a very high level, mainly the supreme headquarters, to allow a unit to cross the border of one corps to another.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But in my opinion, when the 7th Muslim Brigade was going to attack from the south, they was no under command of the 2nd Corps. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When you mentioned about the operations in Vares and the result after, when Vares was taken, would you agree with me that the net result was that 2nd Corps was reunited once again with 1 Corps, 2 Corps, and 3 Corps?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: In my opinion, Vares was attacked from the north by the 2nd Corps; from the west, by the 3rd Corps; and maybe it was also -- with some moment they said 6 Corps, but I have never heard about that before. And also, the 1st Corps. But what I understand, when they take control over Vares, it was more or less by the -- the 7th Muslim Brigade from -- they came from south. In the same moment, you have -- if you look at the map, north-west of Vares in the village of Pogar. Pogar was under control by forces from the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the other Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Kubura, and on behalf of our Defence team I will have a few questions for you regarding some very specific events that you testified about today. Colonel, during your testimony, you said that you were a witness of the events when Croatian civilians were leaving Vares; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I say that a major role when leaving Vares by the Croatian civilians was played by the Croatian authorities of the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I think it was both. They well understand it was under attack. We could hear it. The civilians could hear it. It was shooting a lot. It was grenade impacts in the area. And of course, they also informed them that - what you say - the Muslims was attacking them, and they informed them about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that representatives of the HVO on a loudspeaker system called on the population of Vares to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that this significantly affected the feelings of the population and their fears and their decision to leave the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. They was -- it was a lot of people was afraid. They was escaped. But there was also people that was staying, still, in the city. But some thousands of refugees leave Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony today, you mentioned that when leaving Vares some destroyed their own property. And you gave us an example of a Croat setting fire to his own house. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I only -- it was, what I remember. One family, it was a house north of Bobovac Brigade. It was a very beautiful house. And I think it was a member of the Bobovac Brigade staff. He put it on fire. And I asked him, "Why do you do it?" And he said, "I'm now leaving and I don't want any Muslims should use it." They also put on fire the headquarters in the Sport Hotel. It was also one more house on the opposite side of the road of my camp. But it was not, so to say, destroying. It was only these houses I just described. And it was also one small fire down in the hospital in Vares. But in my opinion, it was some accident where with electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in addition to the events you described a moment ago, the detention of Muslim civilians, that the soldiers of the HVO when leaving Vares were looting the property of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Not what I can remember in this moment. They have been looting down in some Muslims' home some days before down in Vares, but I can't remember it was some looting when they leave. They have do it some days before, and also raped some women there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You have also mentioned that in the operations that took place around Vares that the 2nd and the 3rd Corps of the BiH army took part in those operations; is that true?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: If you mean attacking on Vares, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the 304th Mountain Brigade, 310th Mountain Brigade, the units of the territorial staff of Vares, as well as some units of the 2nd Corps from the direction of north participated in those operations? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: They were attacking Vares area, but they were not inside Vares in which days we are now talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of the fact that the units of the 7th Muslim Brigade, although involved in the operation, did not take part in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No. It was -- what I can understand, I'm only talking about the day when I meet them in Vares. And on this day, it was no HVO units inside Vares. It was empty, so more or less one day ago. And that was also my reason to stop them to shooting inside the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment you told them that there were no members of the HVO in the town itself, the soldiers that you perceived as members of the 7th Brigade started shooting in the air; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. After they have -- when I meet them, they were shooting -- cross-firing on the left side and on the right side of the street, up in the houses. And after I have stopped them and informed them that it was no more HVO soldiers there inside the town, and when they understand that, that's right, there was also some shooting in the area. And it was as I said before some type of celebration. I think it was a big victory for the BH army. And they also then continued to looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: They took this as a victory, a victory without fight.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That is correct. Both yes and no. I mean, this day that was correct. But maybe they have fight the day before against the HVO. But it was no fighting which day inside Vares, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm, sir, that the town of Vares was not exposed to heavy artillery or any shooting in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's right. And we tried -- we negotiate about that a lot of days and informed the BH army it's -- when we are going to attack, don't use it as a revenge for Stupni Do, to shell the town and so on. And in my opinion, they used a lot of artillery but only in the surrounding area. As I remember, it was no impact inside Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the damage was the result of the celebratory shooting.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No, not celebratory shooting. The most was in two phases. The first was going inside Vares. I said before we came along the street in two long columns. They were shooting up in the houses and destroy a lot of windows and houses. And after that, they also destroyed shops and so were cross windows for looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On two occasions you mentioned today that soldiers were interested in food. The soldiers took bread, chocolate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers that came in contact with you, the commander that you spoke to told you that they hadn't seen any food for weeks. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes, weeks or days. I don't remember. But I could see they were hungry. They were tired. And he also informed me that when I tell him that they were not allowed to looting the shops and the UNHCR stores, he said, "That is all logistics." I mean, it was a tactic, a logistic for them, to take what they find.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On direct you said that it was possible, that there may have been some other units in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: What I mean about that is this soldier what I meet in the square, it was, as I say, a member from the 7th Muslim Brigade. I said also before we couldn't be everyplace in the town. And I mean about that if there came more units or soldiers from another unit from the south into the town to -- also looting, I don't know, but I know that this brigade was there in two days and they was stopped by the military police by the BH army that afternoon, the 4th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If I put it to you that the units of the 126th Mountain Brigade, 310th Mountain Brigade, 304th Mountain Brigade, as well as the units of the Territorial Defence of Vares, would you agree with me that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't remember these numbers of brigades. I couldn't -- it's ten years ago, so I don't remember. But I know that it was some type of brigades later I negotiate with in Vares, and they arrived one or two days after these first -- these Muslim soldiers. So it was some type of rotation. They'd take them out and it came another BH soldier. And also it also came soldiers from the 2nd Corps. But it was days later. I don't remember how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the soldiers were also interested in the storage of food that was manned by the UNHCR; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This storage, however, remained intact and all the food remained in the storage; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I was only person, myself, in only one of them, and they have tried to get into it, because it was in a shop. And we stopped it. But what I can remember, I don't think they take something from this, because we concentrate our units there to stop it. And if they take something, it was only small things. I don't remember if they do that. But they tried to do it, and we stop it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: As I was listening to your testimony, would you agree with me that that -- at that moment the situation in the town of Vares itself was chaotic?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes, a little chaotic. That's right. Because -- that's my -- I remember we talked about it in the evening. We said first it was members of HVO who was bad guys, so to say, in the town, looting and raped. And then it came a part of BH army don't rape but were looting. It was first one side and next day -- some days later the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I told you that in such a situation at that moment it was very difficult to control those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Both yes and no. I mean, I successed to speak to them in Swedish, and they clearly understand that they was not allowed to get into a shop with shoes in. So it's on the commander's level to stop things like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the fact that members of the 7th Brigade entered the town of Vares by not obeying their commander's order not to enter the town?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't really understand. Please repeat your ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that members of the 7th Brigade entered the town of Vares of their own will?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No. I've never heard about that. No. Sorry. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the brigade commander, once he had learned that the soldiers were in the town, issued an order for them to leave the town of Vares immediately?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: What I remember, they leave Vares maybe two days later, the 6th of November. And what I can understand as a professional officer, they do it when they have an order of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no further questions from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. The Judges have certain questions. Mr. Mundis, do you have any additional questions? It would be very good if we could finish with this witness today. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just have one or perhaps two questions which arise actually from an abbreviation or an acronym that the witness has used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, listening to your testimony and observing what was appearing in the transcript, is it correct to say that you're using the term "coy" as an abbreviation for company?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you using the term "coy," as an abbreviation for the term company?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Coi, C-o-i, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Coy, in English.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Charlie, October, Yankee.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. So when there were references in the transcript to 8th Mechanised Coy, that should actually be Coy, C-o-y.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel. I'd like to put to you a few follow-up questions on what you told us this morning, the looting of Vares itself. You were a witness to the entrance of the 7th Brigade into Vares from the very first moment?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No. I was not in the south part of Vares. I have a report from the BBC media team that they have observed them and they have take some food and something more for them. They came up to my camp and immediately after that I get together with one of my platoons down to Vares, and we meet this attacking soldier in the square where the mayor's house is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: But when you arrived there, they were still entering the town -- or the village?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: When you arrived there, they were still marching in.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. They were doing a tactic, what infantry do in this type of terrain, shooting cross like this, up in the houses. And it was therefore where I tried to stop them because it was not necessary to shoot and maybe kill civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You talked about the 7th Brigade. That would sound that the whole 7th Brigade was involved. Could you give me an estimate of how many soldiers there were in Vares at that day.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I could only answer what I could see in my own eyes, and it was maybe 100, up to -- a little bit more. But it was also soldier in them all -- more, on both sides of the street in the town. But at the same moment I could only see about 100, up to 150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: But you also heard from your own colleagues in your unit stories about numbers or places or so.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah, in this moment, it was soldier in the whole town. They spread it out, and it was looting everywhere. Every shops and so on. So I don't know exactly how many soldiers. I could only observe about 100, 150 in one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You would say perhaps more than one battalion, or --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: It's very, very difficult to say. But I think it was -- it's also difficult to use these words. Because when I'm talking a battalion, I can look at my own battalion home in Sweden, it was more than 900 soldiers. Here it was brigades down in this area. It's nowhere near 900 soldiers. They used maybe -- wrong words about which type of unit. But if you use company, up to -- I mean, the battalion, maybe it's right number, of some 100 soldiers, what I understand it could be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay. You also told us about a conversation you had with the commander or you had several conversations, I understand. What rank did he have?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't know. He was more or less civilian clothes with some camouflage jacket. And he said he was a battalion commander or -- I don't really remember what he said -- what type of unit he was. He said -- because I pointed out, I said, "Komandant," and he walked forward and at the same moment I was informing to him to stop shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: But you said he was a battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember. It could be -- I don't remember. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And obviously you don't recall his name, do you?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: They never tell us their names. Not in these moments, these situations. Only in moments when I sitting in tables with more conversationable negotiations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, you told us this was the 7th Muslim Brigade. I wonder, was this a conclusion out of the fact that you'd never seen this brigade before or was it based on some other observation?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I have an information from -- also from this BBC team, because they have seen them before, and they said it was them. And I also understand it was some Muslim unit because I've never seen that before, light green flags, a lot of flags, a band on the head with light green, and they were saying "Allah-u-ekber."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you also observe distinctives or insignias or something like that?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Sorry, about ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you also observe distinct emblems or distinct insignias?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You don't remember.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I would like to put you a few questions also on the scale of the looting. You have given an estimate of the number of soldiers that were present. And you have told us that at a certain moment you were engaged in a cat-and-rat play, so to speak. And you tried in vain to stop the loot looting. And then you concentrated on the church and on the stores of the UNHCR, I understand. How long has this process of cat-and-rat playing been pursued? How much time was involved in the process?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: In this looting or ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: How much time were you chasing after the looters or trying to prevent the looting?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: My unit was staying there, whereas to this day. And we stayed there until the French Company arrived at the evening, until one position, and it was the Catholic church. We stayed there, I think, into -- January, February, something like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: But at a certain moment the looting began while you were still trying to prevent it. At another moment, you went to the church and the stores of the UNHCR, because you realised you couldn't stop the process of looting.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's right. Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And how much time was in between there?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: I don't remember. But it could be -- maybe some hour, maybe a little bit more. Because we tried to do it. We was also shooting in there with some places. But they stop when we was there. When we go to another place, we have reporting we need more help; they were looting. We get there, when we went back that this situation, they start looting again. And so I understand after maybe an hour, that it is not necessary for us to running, running, running around the town to stop it. You must concentrate it to these places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: There was some discussion earlier on, on the things that were looting and the question especially related to food. Were other things looted, or was it a question of only taking food from various shops?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, in the small shop it was chocolate, newspapers, pens, and so on. And when I break it up, there also took pens and so on. And they -- wanted to give me one, but I said, "No, thank you." So they take what they find. But especially I understand they were -- I could understand they were hungry, and they also inform me that it's all logistics to find food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And later on in the day it remained food? Or it became also other objects, like refrigerators or whatever else, electric equipment you may have?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. If we're beginning in Kopjari, the 21st of October, when they tried to put the civilians out. The next day, the 22nd of October, I have a report from my soldiers up there that they start looting the village. We have also earlier observed that they were looting in Ratanj. And so after Vares was taken under control of BH army, we again have a report from the observers post up in Kopjari that it was trucks and cars with equipment from houses. It was furniture, it was refrigerators and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you observe that too at this day in November in Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Not that day. As I say, I was only there to give an order to take this position at the church. I was in one of the stores and talked to the BH soldier that you're not allowed to use it and we are going to shoot you if you enter this place. After that, I have a report on my radio there was some massacre or something like this up in the village of Pogar. So I leave Vares and get up there with a patrol --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You talked about this already.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: About the looting itself, did you also or any member of your unit observe that private houses were looted, not only shops?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: As I say, I can only remember what I could observe now. It was most things shops on the main street they looted. But we also observed trucks and cars when they threw it away. That must be also by private homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay. Some questions still on the afternoon. On the one hand you told us that there was a unit from Sarajevo coming to reinforce you, a French Battalion or a French unit.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And on the other hand you said that the looting was stopped by the 3rd army, members of the 3rd army, I suppose the military police. I don't know. What is the relationship between the two? If you say "We got reinforcements from the French from Sarajevo," implying that you had a need for it, then you may also think as a listener that this was the event that stopped the looting.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yeah. We asked for help before, when we tried to get into Stupni Do. We also have help from the BritBat. We were -- one mechanised company. And they have now get back to Vitez. And my commander was down in Sarajevo, so I think, if I remember right, they start leaving Sarajevo at the morning or something like this, when we have this reporting, when it was going on again inside Vares. And they arrived at the evening of this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And then the looting had stopped already.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: What I can remember, it was stopped end of afternoon by military police from the BH army. I don't know if they came from the 3rd Corps. It was from the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did it resume the following day, or was that the final end of it?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes, it was still fighting outside Vares, especially in the area of Dastansko, were the rest of the Bobovac Brigade was put together now, a small pocket. It was the next day very calm in Vares. And what I can remember the next day, that means the 6th of November, the Muslim brigade left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: But in between that time, there was no looting.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Not that I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you observe the moment the 7th Brigade left Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: No. I don't observe that. We have -- what I can remember, it was some rotation. It came as other units. I remember one of the officers I talked to have a sign, "Vares." Maybe it was the name of a unit from the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So you're not in a position to -- to state whether or not things were taken with the 3rd Brigade, looted things, accompanied the 7 Brigade in leaving Vares.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: What -- what brigade? The 7th -- sorry, what corps the 7th Brigade was -- belonged to, I don't know. And what I remember was that they leave after one to two days after they have arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: No. My question is simply: Did the 7th Brigade take looted goods with them on cars or buses or trucks or something? You didn't observe that, I understand.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Not that I observed and remember now when they leave. Maybe they have done it before because we saw. But no. But I can't say that they do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one military question for you. You've told us that you saw them lined in two columns, and you've also told us that this was a customary tactic, that soldiers would move in two columns. One was shooting at the walls on you left-hand side. Now, this happened quite a number of years ago. Do you remember whether these people, some 100 people that were there, had at their disposal a radio set or a walkie-talkie? Did they have radio communication with the higher authorities, that is, their superiors who were outside of that area? Theoretically speaking, in every corps of a well-organised army there's always a radio communication. As far as you can remember, did these people have some sort of a communication, radio communication with their superiors, or were they totally on their own?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: What I can remember: Normally you don't have this radio communication in the front, in the first soldiers. They are more back. And I can't say that they had so, because I cannot remember that I could observe that they had some radio communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just complete my question. According to you, those who were in those two columns believed they were still members of the HVO. They were, according to their own belief, in a typical military situation. And in such a situation, there is a radio communication with the superiors outside of the territory. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: Yes. Normally they -- I think they have so. Because we have observed that we have small, what you carry, not walkie-talkie but something like this. But I couldn't observe that -- not what I can remember in this soldier in the front here. And I also have to say that normally in my army we don't have a communication in the front. So maybe they have it more back in this unit. But I can't remember I could observe that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, do you have any additional questions for this witness? Are there any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, we don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor. We have already extended our time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one or two questions arising from questions put to the witness by Judge Swart.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Colonel, you said that shortly after Vares was -- or this looting that was observed occurred in Vares, one of your observation posts in Kopjari reported vehicles carrying looted goods; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Towards which direction were these vehicles coming and in which direction were they vehicles going?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER
utterances.text: From east to west; that means from the road from Vares-Pogar in the direction of Ratanj and Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has already replied; however, the question that was put by my learned friend was the subject of the examination-in-chief already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We have taken note of your observation. If there are no other questions, we would like to thank you, sir, for having come here to give your testimony. We wish you a safe journey back home. I would like to ask the usher to take you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Withopf, tomorrow it seems that we will have a problem. The witness that was envisaged for Wednesday cannot be heard tomorrow. Can you please clarify and tell us what we have now as a result of the new elements that you have told us about earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, for this purpose, could we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Registrar, can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 2nd day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
